price.notes: VERIFIED BBY 18197449: reg $3,229, sale $2,479. Includes 288GB dock add-on per listing title.

offers.name: HP Envy x360 16" WUXGA Touchscreen 2-in-1 Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 7 155U - 64GB LPDDR5 - 2TB SSD+288GB - Win 11 Pro - Silver

reviews.quote: Priced well for an upper-mid-tier device with a gorgeous display and solid performance — creators will love this laptop's flexible form factor and impressive battery life.

praises: 64GB RAM in a sub-$2,500 convertible — unmatched for VMs, huge spreadsheets, and tab hoarding
2TB storage + 288GB dock bundle included at the sale price
Windows 11 Pro with BitLocker/Remote Desktop for home-office users
Big 16" touch canvas with full ports incl. HDMI + 2x USB-A
Quiet fans; 155U barely heats during office work
complaints: 155U CPU is the weak link — 64GB of RAM can't fix a 12-core low-power chip
Heavy (~2 kg) and thick for a convertible — tablet mode is a token feature
Base WUXGA 60Hz glossy panel undersells the premium spec sheet
No Thunderbolt on this tier; USB-C limited to DP/PD
Regular price $3,229 is notional — only the sale price is real

design_philosophy: The outlier of the Envy x360 16 range: a RAM-max configuration (64GB) aimed at power users who want workstation memory in a family-priced chassis, even though the 155U CPU and 60Hz panel cap what that memory can do.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from Envy x360 16 anchor (entry 34): +0.5 productivity and +0.5 ai_ml for 64GB (local LLM headroom), per cross-config inference rules. CPU remains the ceiling — noted in complaints. No pro review of exact CA config (bot-walls, SHARED-hp-convertibles.md).
